BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer review of Seller update and Disclosure Letter

**Threshold points**
- The Seller's labels ([STANDARD], "FINAL", "agreed at principal level", "cleared by both sides", "market standard") are assertions. Nothing in our file shows Amelia Frost approved any of them, so I have reviewed every clause on its merits.
- The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts parts of its cover narrative (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, incident, title).
- Two Seller numbers match our fallbacks (AUD 4.8m cap, 18 months). That does not clear them. Both need Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and hold at AUD 6.0m. Reason: 20% is a conditional fallback usable only with Amelia Frost's written authority, which we don't have, so we can't concede it.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with liability from the first dollar once exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** Reject and restore our figures and the first-dollar mechanism. Reason: the Seller's thresholds are 5x higher, and the deductible structure removes recovery for many realistic claims.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months, plus a statement that "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims, with the limitation wording confined to general claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Hold at 24 months and delete the "all Claims" override. Reason: 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval (none given), and the override would silently shorten Title, Fraud and other regimes.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties get the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** A separate Fundamental/Title regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Reason: "administrative simplicity" would cap title claims at about 20% and 18 months, which is unacceptable for a 100% share purchase.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** None. Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert an express carve-out in each of those clauses. Reason: this is non-waivable, and the Seller's wording would currently shield even fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** Deemed disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sched 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the general disclosures (1.1, 1.2). Accept only specific disclosures that are fair and clear. Reason: whole-data-room and public-register disclosure would hollow out the warranties. Para 1.4 (no admissions) should not cut across the warranties or indemnities.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any qualifier must use named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and never apply to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3. Reason: it combines buyer-knowledge and constructive-knowledge exclusions, and would defeat the specific indemnities and fraud claims.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (about AUD 3.6m, about 30% of revenue)**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, and the consent is treated as satisfied on delivery of the written consent.
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions (DD-002 cl 11.3) are satisfied, before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make it a hard condition precedent covering both the consent and evidence of satisfied conditions. Reason: the Seller's own letter (para 2) admits no consent and no evidence exist, and reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a customer of this size.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (about AUD 3.2m)**
- **Seller:** A release to be provided after Completion.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Require a payout letter, repayment direct to Riverlark from the funds flow, and releases delivered at Completion. Reason: the letter (para 3) confirms the facility is unrepaid with no discharge. A post-completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)**
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 is "a matter for the Seller" and is not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or an express Seller-funded obligation.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the silent exclusion. Add a line item or a price deduction or indemnity, and ask the Seller to confirm payroll tax, super and other on-costs. Reason: the Seller's letter (para 5) admits the amounts are absent from the funds flow and is silent on on-costs, so Paperbark would otherwise bear the cost after Completion.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A broader IP indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure (payment of every SOW3 fee under DD-004 cl 7.3, then transfer of Project Materials).
- **Recommendation:** Broaden the indemnity to cover related IP ownership, assignment and third-party claims, and require a payment receipt and confirmatory assignment. Reason: the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way (the DD-010 record is not bank verification), and no assignment exists in the data room.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sched 6).
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, an investigation, and regular updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** Do not adopt the Seller's materiality characterisation. Add covenants for log preservation, investigation, prompt updates and cooperation. Keep it neutral, with no loss figure or breach conclusion either way. Reason: the letter itself says access, scope and notification are unresolved (about 1,240 records), so "not material" is unsupported. Our position should be protective without asserting a breach.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000: 3 × AUD 110,000)**
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment of the renewals, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the characterisation and do not treat the amount as Debt either. Request the contracts (DD-008, DD-011), and confirm terminability, accrual and timing, then decide treatment. Reason: the Seller's letter (para 8) doesn't say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, so neither side's label is verified.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Everything is folded into the general regime, with limitations applying to "all Claims" unless expressly stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Redraft the limitation clauses so the general limits apply only to general Warranty Claims, with each category having its own regime. Reason: the "all Claims" language is a back-door override of the specific regimes.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority.
- **Recommendation:** Reject reliance on DD-012 alone. Require independent evidence such as ASIC extracts, transfer and ownership history, encumbrance and PPSR searches, and authority and approval documents, plus a Title warranty under the Fundamental regime. Reason: the register is a Company-supplied internal source, and the letter (para 10) concedes the Buyer hasn't verified it.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Both remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled" and mark both OPEN. Reason: nothing has been agreed, and treating them as closed would lock in the 20%/18-month general limits without authority.

---

**Next steps**
1. Ask Amelia Frost whether any principal-level agreement exists. No fallback (20% cap, 18 months) should be offered without her written authority identifying this draft.
2. Send the mark-up with a note that no [STANDARD] or FINAL label is accepted and that all clauses remain under review.
3. Issue a supplementary DD request covering:
   - Bluefen consent and conditions
   - Riverlark payout figure and discharge documents
   - Ironquay payment evidence
   - Bonus on-costs
   - DD-006 logs and investigation status
   - Sandbar contracts
   - Independent title evidence
